title: SB 2608 (2022 Regular Session): Affidavit ballots; reduce length of time within which certain persons must present proper voter ID or execute religious exemption.
operative_text:
(a_in_person_id)
(section) Sec. 1 (23-15-563(1))
(quote) Each person who appears to vote in person at a polling place or the registrar's office shall be required to identify himself or herself to a poll manager or the registrar by presenting current and valid photo identification before such person shall be allowed to vote.
(section) Sec. 1 (23-15-563(2))
(quote) (a) A current and valid Mississippi driver's license; (b) A current and valid identification card issued by a branch, department, agency or entity of the State of Mississippi; (c) A current and valid United States passport;
(b_no_id_remedy)
(section) Sec. 1 (23-15-563(3)(a))
(quote) A person who appears to vote in person at a polling place and does not have identification as required by this section may vote by affidavit ballot. The affidavit ballot shall then be counted if the person shall present acceptable photo identification to the registrar within * * * three (3) days.
(section) Sec. 1 (23-15-563(3)(b))
(quote) An elector who has a religious objection to being photographed may vote by affidavit ballot, and the elector, within * * * three (3) days after the election, shall execute an affidavit in the registrar's office affirming that the exemption applies.
(section) Sec. 2 (23-15-573(2)(d))
(quote) An affidavit ballot of a voter who was unable to present an acceptable form of photo identification shall not be rejected for this reason if the voter does either of the following: (i) Returns to the circuit clerk's office, or to the municipal clerk's office for municipal elections, within * * * three (3) business days after the date of the election and presents an acceptable form of photo identification;
(section) Sec. 2 (23-15-573(2)(b))
(quote) then the poll manager shall write "NO ID" across from the voter's name and in the appropriate column in the pollbook.
(c_mail_ballot_id) not stated.
(d_proof_of_citizenship) not stated.
(e_other_rule)
(section) Sec. 1 (23-15-563(4))
(quote) The intentional failure of an election official to require a voter to present identification as required by this section shall be considered corrupt conduct under Section 97-13-19 and shall be reported to the Secretary of State and the Attorney General.
(other) Sec. 2 (23-15-573): affidavit ballot procedure reprinted; ID-less voters get written notice of how to learn if the ballot counted; uniform affidavit envelope; statewide tracking by reason
